title: Listening and speaking demo (German)
description: Try listening and speaking practice: a dialogue played line by line, listening and dictation questions, a speaking exercise where you record yourself and compare, and words with recorded pronunciation.
author: Erudior

lessons.title: Im Café: listen and speak
lessons.body:
## Listen to the dialogue

Press **Play all** to hear the whole conversation, or 🔊 to hear one line. The first two lines play a recording; the others use your device's German voice. Turn on **Hide the words** to listen first, then read.

```dialogue lang=de-DE
# Im Café
Kellner: Guten Tag! Was möchten Sie trinken?
= Hello! What would you like to drink?
audio: data:audio/mpeg;base64,
Anna: Einen Kaffee, bitte.
= A coffee, please.
audio: data:audio/mpeg;base64,
Kellner: Mit Milch und Zucker?
= With milk and sugar?
Anna: Nur mit Milch, danke.
= Just with milk, thanks.
```

## Say it yourself

Listen to each phrase, record yourself saying it, then press **Compare** to hear the model and then you. Try again until you sound alike.

```speak lang=de-DE
# Introduce yourself and order
Ich heiße Anna.
= My name is Anna.
audio: data:audio/mpeg;base64,
Wie heißt du?
= What's your name?
Einen Kaffee, bitte.
= A coffee, please.
audio: data:audio/mpeg;base64,
```

> **Note:** The recordings in this demo were made with a computer voice (espeak-ng). Real courses use recordings of native speakers.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the waiter ask?

audio.text: Guten Tag! Was möchten Sie trinken?

choices: What would you like to drink?
What would you like to eat?
questions.explanation: "Was möchten Sie trinken?" means "What would you like to drink?" (trinken = to drink).

questions.stem: Listen and type what you hear.
questions.explanation: "Ich trinke gern Tee" means "I like drinking tea." Nouns like Tee start with a capital letter.
"Das Wasser ist kalt" means "The water is cold." This one uses your device's German voice.
